analysis:
Integrated all 22 units. The PR is a Gemma 4 tokenizer byte-fallback fix. The only executable change is LocalTokenizerBridge in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/LocalTokenizerLoader.swift (head ~lines 68-139). It adds heldBackBytes, probed once at init with 256 convertTokenToId/convertIdToToken lookups, and decode now appends a trailing run of `<0xHH>` tokens that swift-transformers' ByteFallbackDecoder would drop. Invalid UTF-8 is repaired to U+FFFD through String(decoding:as:). The rest is documentation (changelog.d/gemma-byte-fallback-flush.md, docs/architecture/inference.md, docs/developer/test.md) and a new test file (LocalTokenizerByteFallbackTests.swift).

Security analysis: the change adds no network, file, crypto, key, attestation, authorization, routing or cache-scope behavior. Decoding happens after decryption inside the provider process, and output still goes through the existing encrypted response path (T-008, A-001). No new logging or persistence appears in the supplied patch. Prefix-cache keys, token IDs and cache scoping (T-041) are unchanged. The changelog says only that a stop string completed by a trailing run can match one token earlier, so completion_tokens can fall by one. That is a minor usage-count nuance, not a billing-integrity issue. The coordinator's token accounting was not examined.

DoS and bounds: the reverse scan in decode stops at the first non-byte token that decodes non-empty. With skipSpecialTokens it may call upstream.decode per skipped special token, so cost is linear in the run length. Tokenizer files are operator-controlled and were already trusted before this PR (T-012 and A-004 are pre-existing), so a malicious tokenizer can only alter output text.

Coverage limits: omitted integration source units were not replayed. The test file contents and upstream swift-transformers and DetokenizerV2 behavior were not seen, so those are inferred from comments and docs. No security regression found.
